# Sensitivity analyses {#sec-sensitivity}

*Script: `Code/40_sensitivity_analyses.R`. Tables:
`Output/Tables/sensitivity_adjustment_or.csv`,
`sensitivity_adjustment_interaction.csv`, `sensitivity_reference_or.csv`,
`sensitivity_reference_interaction.csv` and `sensitivity_ozone_series.csv`.*

```{r}
#| label: setup-sensitivity
#| include: false
source(here::here("Code", "00_setup.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "01_functions.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "02_plot_style.R"))
library(knitr)
theme_set(theme_report())
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

read_table <- function(file) fread(file.path(dir_tables, file), encoding = "UTF-8")
fmt <- function(x, digits = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
ci <- function(estimate, low, high, digits = 3) {
  sprintf("%s (%s to %s)", fmt(estimate, digits), fmt(low, digits), fmt(high, digits))
}
as_numeric_columns <- function(dt, pattern) {
  columns <- grep(pattern, names(dt), value = TRUE)
  dt[, (columns) := lapply(.SD, as.numeric), .SDcols = columns]
  dt[]
}
lag_main <- get_param("models", "lag_main")
heatwave_main <- get_param("models", "heatwave_main")
cutoff_main <- get_param("models", "ozone_cutoff_main")
low_cutoff <- get_param("sensitivity", "low_ozone_cutoff")
increments <- get_param("sensitivity", "adjustment_increments")
temperature <- get_param("temperature_response")

adjusted_or <- read_table("sensitivity_adjustment_or.csv")
adjusted_int <- as_numeric_columns(read_table("sensitivity_adjustment_interaction.csv"),
                                   "^(estimate|low|high)$")
reference_or <- read_table("sensitivity_reference_or.csv")
reference_int <- as_numeric_columns(read_table("sensitivity_reference_interaction.csv"),
                                    "^(estimate|low|high)$")
series_fits <- as_numeric_columns(read_table("sensitivity_ozone_series.csv"),
                                  "^(estimate|low|high|or)_")

pollutant_labels <- c(pm25 = "PM2.5", no2 = "NO2", hum = "relative humidity",
                      temperature = "temperature")
adjustment_label <- function(x) {
  vapply(strsplit(x, " + ", fixed = TRUE), function(keys) {
    if (identical(keys, "none")) "No adjustment" else paste("+", paste(pollutant_labels[keys],
                                                                      collapse = ", "))
  }, character(1))
}
adjustment_levels <- adjustment_label(unique(adjusted_or$adjustment))
headline <- adjusted_or[outcome == "non_accidental" & lag == lag_main]
or_of <- function(adjustment_value, term_value) {
  headline[adjustment == adjustment_value & term == term_value, ci(or, or_low, or_high)]
}
all_pollutants <- paste(names(increments), collapse = " + ")
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Preliminary

Every analysis starts from the working definitions of the
[main models](deliverable_3_models.html#sec-models): heatwave
`r heatwave_label(heatwave_main)` and
ozone above the `r cutoff_main`th percentile of the municipality in the
delivered series. One element changes at a time.
:::

## Adjustment for other pollutants and humidity

The compound model is refitted with PM2.5, nitrogen dioxide and relative
humidity as continuous covariates, each at the same lag as the exposure, one
at a time and together. The covariates are the municipal series delivered
with the ozone series (24-hour means, IDW). All the variants use the same
deaths: the `r fmt(unique(headline$deaths), 0)` non-accidental deaths whose
referent days have every covariate
(`r fmt(unique(headline$deaths_dropped), 0)` are left out).

```{r}
#| label: fig-adjustment
#| fig-cap: !expr 'sprintf("Odds ratios of non-accidental death by exposure category and adjustment, lag %d. Bars are 95%% confidence intervals.", lag_main)'
#| fig-height: 4
plot_data <- headline[term %in% names(category_labels)]
plot_data[, `:=`(category = category_factor(term),
                 adjusted_for = factor(adjustment_label(adjustment), levels = rev(adjustment_levels)))]
ggplot(plot_data, aes(or, adjusted_for, colour = category)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, colour = ink$axis) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = or_low, xmax = or_high), linewidth = 0.6, size = 0.35) +
  facet_wrap(~category, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colour_compound[levels(plot_data$category)], guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Odds ratio", y = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-adjustment
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'sprintf("Odds ratios (95%% confidence interval) by adjustment, lag %d.", lag_main)'
table_data <- adjusted_or[lag == lag_main & term %in% names(category_labels)]
table_data[, `:=`(cause = cause_labels[outcome], category = category_factor(term),
                  adjusted_for = factor(adjustment_label(adjustment), levels = adjustment_levels),
                  value = ci(or, or_low, or_high))]
kable(dcast(table_data, cause + adjusted_for ~ category, value.var = "value"),
      col.names = c("Cause", "Adjusted for", levels(table_data$category)))
```

With the three covariates together the odds ratio of high-ozone-only days
goes from `r or_of("none", "e01")` to `r or_of(all_pollutants, "e01")`, that
of heatwave-only days from `r or_of("none", "e10")` to
`r or_of(all_pollutants, "e10")` and that of days with both from
`r or_of("none", "e11")` to `r or_of(all_pollutants, "e11")`. Once PM2.5,
nitrogen dioxide and humidity are in the model, the odds ratio of high ozone
alone cannot be told apart from 1; the odds ratios of heatwave days are
smaller and their intervals still exclude 1.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-covariates
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'sprintf("Odds ratios of the covariates, non-accidental mortality, lag %d.", lag_main)'
covariates <- headline[term %in% names(increments)]
covariates[, `:=`(adjusted_for = factor(adjustment_label(adjustment), levels = adjustment_levels),
                  covariate = sprintf("%s, per %s %s", pollutant_labels[term], increment,
                                      c(pm25 = "µg/m³", no2 = "ppb",
                                        hum = "percentage points")[term]),
                  value = ci(or, or_low, or_high))]
kable(covariates[order(adjusted_for), .(adjusted_for, covariate, value)],
      col.names = c("Model", "Covariate", "Odds ratio (95% CI)"))
```

### Interaction after adjustment

```{r}
#| label: fig-adjustment-reoi
#| fig-cap: "REOI by adjustment and lag. Bars are 95% confidence intervals; zero means no additive interaction."
#| fig-height: 5.2
reoi <- adjusted_int[measure == "REOI"]
reoi[, `:=`(cause = factor(cause_labels[outcome], levels = cause_labels[unique(outcome)]),
            adjusted_for = factor(adjustment_label(adjustment), levels = rev(adjustment_levels)))]
ggplot(reoi, aes(estimate, adjusted_for)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = ink$axis) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = low, xmax = high), colour = ramp_blue[6], linewidth = 0.5, size = 0.3) +
  facet_grid(cause ~ paste("Lag", lag)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(-0.1, 0, 0.1)) +
  labs(x = "REOI", y = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: reoi-range
reoi_range <- reoi[, .(lowest = min(estimate), highest = max(estimate),
                       excluding_zero = sum(low > 0 | high < 0), fits = .N)]
```

The REOI stays between `r fmt(reoi_range$lowest, 3)` and
`r fmt(reoi_range$highest, 3)` across the `r reoi_range$fits` combinations of
cause, lag and adjustment, and its 95% interval
`r if (reoi_range$excluding_zero == 0) "includes zero in all of them" else sprintf("excludes zero in %d of them", reoi_range$excluding_zero)`.

## Adjustment for temperature

This analysis is not in the plan. The heatwave indicator is a threshold on
temperature, and ozone is higher on hot days, so part of the odds ratio of
high-ozone days may be temperature below the heatwave threshold. The compound
model is refitted with the daily maximum temperature of the same day, as a
natural cubic spline of its percentile among the warm-season days of the
municipality (knots at the `r paste0(temperature$spline_knots, "th", collapse = " and ")`
percentiles). Percentiles are used because the municipal temperature series
are area means whose level differs by more than 10 °C between municipalities.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-temperature-adjustment
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'sprintf("Compound model adjusted for the temperature of the same day, non-accidental mortality, lag %d.", lag_main)'
temperature_rows <- headline[adjustment %in% c("none", "temperature",
                                               paste(c(names(increments), "temperature"), collapse = " + "))]
temperature_rows[, `:=`(adjusted_for = factor(adjustment_label(adjustment), levels = adjustment_levels),
                        row = fifelse(term %in% names(category_labels), category_labels[term],
                                      sub("temperature_p", "Temperature, percentile ", term)),
                        value = ci(or, or_low, or_high))]
temperature_rows <- temperature_rows[term %in% names(category_labels) | grepl("^temperature_p", term)]
temperature_rows[grepl("^Temperature", row), row := paste(row, "against", temperature$reference)]
kable(dcast(temperature_rows, factor(row, levels = unique(row)) ~ adjusted_for, value.var = "value"),
      col.names = c("Term", levels(droplevels(temperature_rows$adjusted_for))))
```

With temperature in the model the heatwave indicator measures what heatwave
days add beyond the temperature of the day itself, a different question from
the one of the plan. Read that way, days with both exposures keep an odds
ratio of `r or_of("temperature", "e11")`, heatwave-only days
`r or_of("temperature", "e10")` and high-ozone-only days
`r or_of("temperature", "e01")`.

## Reference category: three ozone levels

The plan words the reference category as "non-heatwave day and low ozone
(at or below the 50th percentile)" and the exposed categories with ozone above
the 75th percentile. The headline model splits the days at one cut-off, so its
reference includes the days between the two percentiles. Here ozone has three
levels: low (at or below the `r low_cutoff`th percentile), medium and high
(above the `r cutoff_main`th), and the reference is no heatwave with low ozone.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-reference
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'sprintf("Odds ratios with three ozone levels, non-accidental mortality, lag %d. Reference: no heatwave and low ozone.", lag_main)'
r <- reference_or[outcome == "non_accidental" & lag == lag_main]
r[, `:=`(heatwave_day = fifelse(heatwave == 1, "Heatwave", "No heatwave"),
         level = factor(ozone_level, levels = c("low", "medium", "high")),
         value = ci(or, or_low, or_high))]
reference_row <- data.table(heatwave_day = "No heatwave", level = factor("low", levels = levels(r$level)),
                            deaths = unique(r$deaths_reference), value = "1 (reference)")
r <- rbind(r[, .(heatwave_day, level, deaths, value)], reference_row)
setorder(r, -heatwave_day, level)
kable(r, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Heatwave", "Ozone level", "Deaths", "Odds ratio (95% CI)"))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-reference-reoi
#| tbl-cap: "REOI with three ozone levels: high ozone and medium ozone, each against low ozone."
ri <- reference_int[measure == "REOI"]
ri[, `:=`(cause = cause_labels[outcome], value = ci(estimate, low, high))]
kable(dcast(ri, cause + contrast ~ paste("Lag", lag), value.var = "value"),
      col.names = c("Cause", "Contrast", paste("Lag", sort(unique(ri$lag)))))
```

```{r}
#| label: reference-text
h1_low <- reference_or[outcome == "non_accidental" & lag == lag_main & term == "h1_low"]
```

The conclusion does not change. Heatwave days with low ozone are few
(`r fmt(h1_low$deaths, 0)` deaths), so their odds ratio,
`r ci(h1_low$or, h1_low$or_low, h1_low$or_high)`, is less precise than in
the headline model.

## Ozone series

The same model with each ozone series of the exposure dataset: the delivered
series in its two versions (values within the operational period of each
monitor, and all values), the 24-hour mean rebuilt from the validated hourly
records and the daily maximum 8-hour mean (MDA8), each interpolated by IDW and
by ordinary kriging. The cut-off is always the `r cutoff_main`th percentile of
the municipality.

```{r}
#| label: fig-series
#| fig-cap: "REOI by ozone series and lag, non-accidental mortality. Bars are 95% confidence intervals."
#| fig-height: 4.2
series_levels <- unique(series_fits$series_label)
s <- series_fits[outcome == "non_accidental"]
s[, series_label := factor(series_label, levels = rev(series_levels))]
ggplot(s, aes(estimate_reoi, series_label)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = ink$axis) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = low_reoi, xmax = high_reoi), colour = ramp_blue[6],
                  linewidth = 0.5, size = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~paste("Lag", lag), nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "REOI", y = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-series
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'sprintf("Odds ratios and REOI (95%% confidence interval) by ozone series, non-accidental mortality, lag %d.", lag_main)'
st <- series_fits[outcome == "non_accidental" & lag == lag_main,
             .(series_label, deaths_e11,
               e01 = ci(or_e01, or_low_e01, or_high_e01), e10 = ci(or_e10, or_low_e10, or_high_e10),
               e11 = ci(or_e11, or_low_e11, or_high_e11),
               reoi = ci(estimate_reoi, low_reoi, high_reoi))]
kable(st, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Ozone series", "Deaths on days with both", category_labels[["e01"]],
                    category_labels[["e10"]], category_labels[["e11"]], "REOI"))
```

```{r}
#| label: series-range
series_range <- series_fits[, .(lowest = min(estimate_reoi), highest = max(estimate_reoi),
                           excluding_zero = sum(low_reoi > 0 | high_reoi < 0), fits = .N)]
```

Across the `r series_range$fits` fits (two causes, eight series, four lags) the
REOI ranges from `r fmt(series_range$lowest, 3)` to `r fmt(series_range$highest, 3)`
and its 95% interval
`r if (series_range$excluding_zero == 0) "includes zero in all of them" else sprintf("excludes zero in %d of them", series_range$excluding_zero)`. The
choice between the delivered series and the series rebuilt from the hourly
records, or between IDW and kriging, changes which days are classified as
high ozone
([validation of the ozone exposure](deliverable_1_exposure.html#sec-ozone-validation))
but not the answer to the interaction question.

## Heatwave and ozone definitions

The grid of the 15 heatwave definitions and the ozone cut-offs is in
[deliverable 3](deliverable_3_models.html#sec-grid). The lags 2 and 3 of that
grid, where part of the cells show a positive REOI, are examined in the
[lag structure](#sec-lag-structure) below.

# Lag structure: all the lags in one model {#sec-lag-structure}

*Script: `Code/41_distributed_lag_models.R`. Tables:
`Output/Tables/lags_compound_or.csv`, `lags_compound_interaction.csv`,
`lags_grid.csv`, `lags_temperature_or.csv`, `lags_temperature_curve.csv` and
`lags_ozone_or.csv`. For comparison: `models_main_or.csv` and `models_grid.csv`
of `Code/30_models_main.R`.*

```{r}
#| label: setup-lag-structure
#| include: false
source(here::here("Code", "00_setup.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "01_functions.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "02_plot_style.R"))
library(knitr)
theme_set(theme_report())
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

read_table <- function(file) fread(file.path(dir_tables, file), encoding = "UTF-8")
fmt <- function(x, digits = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
ci <- function(estimate, low, high, digits = 3) {
  sprintf("%s (%s to %s)", fmt(estimate, digits), fmt(low, digits), fmt(high, digits))
}
as_numeric_columns <- function(dt, pattern) {
  columns <- grep(pattern, names(dt), value = TRUE)
  dt[, (columns) := lapply(.SD, as.numeric), .SDcols = columns]
  dt[]
}
lags <- unlist(get_param("design", "lags_days"))
heatwave_main <- get_param("models", "heatwave_main")
cutoff_main <- get_param("models", "ozone_cutoff_main")
ozone_series <- paste0(get_param("air_pollution", "ozone_series_main"), "_",
                       get_param("air_pollution", "interpolation_method_main"))
ozone_flag_main <- paste0(ozone_series, "_gt_p", cutoff_main)
temperature <- get_param("temperature_response")
ozone_increment <- get_param("distributed_lags", "ozone_increment_ppb")

main_or <- read_table("models_main_or.csv")
lag_or <- read_table("lags_compound_or.csv")
lag_int <- as_numeric_columns(read_table("lags_compound_interaction.csv"), "^(estimate|low|high)$")
lag_grid <- as_numeric_columns(read_table("lags_grid.csv"), "^(estimate|low|high|or)_")
single_grid <- as_numeric_columns(read_table("models_grid.csv"), "^(estimate|low|high|or)_")
thresholds <- read_table("temperature_thresholds.csv")
temperature_or <- read_table("lags_temperature_or.csv")
curve <- read_table("lags_temperature_curve.csv")
ozone_or <- read_table("lags_ozone_or.csv")
colour_model <- c("One lag per model" = "#2a78d6", "All lags in one model" = "#eb6834")
lag_levels <- c(lags, "cumulative")
lag_factor <- function(x) factor(x, levels = lag_levels, labels = c(lags, "Cumulative"))
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Preliminary

Working definitions as in the
[main models](deliverable_3_models.html#sec-models): heatwave
`r heatwave_label(heatwave_main)`, ozone above the `r cutoff_main`th percentile
of the municipality in the delivered series. The form in which temperature
enters the models of this section is a proposal, marked `TO CONFIRM` in
`config/config.yml`.
:::

## Why

The models of deliverable 3 and of the sensitivity analyses take one lag at a
time: the exposure of the day of death, or of one, two or three days before.
Exposures of consecutive days are not independent. A heatwave lasts at least
two days by definition and
ozone episodes last several days, so the odds ratio of the exposure two days
before also carries the effect of the exposure one day before and on the day.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-persistence
#| tbl-cap: "Persistence of the exposure: of the municipality-days in each state, share (%) in the same state one, two and three days before. Referent days of the case-crossover dataset."
columns <- c(paste0(heatwave_main, "_lag", lags), paste0(ozone_flag_main, "_lag", lags))
x <- fread(derived_path("exposure_lagged.csv"), select = columns)
hw <- function(k) x[[paste0(heatwave_main, "_lag", k)]]
oz <- function(k) x[[paste0(ozone_flag_main, "_lag", k)]]
persistence <- rbindlist(lapply(setdiff(lags, 0), function(k) data.table(
  days_before = k,
  heatwave = 100 * mean(hw(k)[hw(0) == 1] == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
  high_ozone = 100 * mean(oz(k)[oz(0) == 1] == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
  both = 100 * mean((hw(k) == 1 & oz(k) == 1)[hw(0) == 1 & oz(0) == 1], na.rm = TRUE)
)))
kable(persistence, digits = 0,
      col.names = c("Days before", "Heatwave", "High ozone", "Heatwave and high ozone"))
```

In this section the exposures of the four lags enter the same model, with one
coefficient per lag and no constraint on their shape. Each lag-specific odds
ratio is then adjusted for the other lags, and the sum of the coefficients
gives a cumulative odds ratio over the window.

## Exposure categories

```{r}
#| label: fig-compound
#| fig-cap: "Odds ratios of non-accidental death by exposure category and lag: one lag per model (deliverable 3) and all the lags in one model. Bars are 95% confidence intervals."
#| fig-height: 4.2
single <- main_or[outcome == "non_accidental" & subgroup == "all" & model == "compound",
                  .(category = term, lag = as.character(lag), or, or_low, or_high,
                    model = "One lag per model")]
together <- lag_or[outcome == "non_accidental", .(category, lag, or, or_low, or_high,
                                                 model = "All lags in one model")]
both <- rbind(single, together)
both[, `:=`(category = category_factor(category), lag = lag_factor(lag),
            model = factor(model, levels = names(colour_model)))]
ggplot(both, aes(lag, or, colour = model)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = ink$axis) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = or_low, ymax = or_high), position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
                  linewidth = 0.6, size = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~category, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colour_model) +
  labs(x = "Lag (days)", y = "Odds ratio", colour = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-compound
#| tbl-cap: "Odds ratios (95% confidence interval) with all the lags in one model."
t1 <- copy(lag_or)
t1[, `:=`(cause = cause_labels[outcome], category = category_factor(category),
          lag = lag_factor(lag), value = ci(or, or_low, or_high))]
kable(dcast(t1, cause + lag ~ category, value.var = "value"),
      col.names = c("Cause", "Lag", levels(t1$category)))
```

```{r}
#| label: compound-text
na <- lag_or[outcome == "non_accidental"]
pick <- function(category_value, lag_value) {
  na[category == category_value & lag == lag_value, ci(or, or_low, or_high)]
}
later <- na[lag %in% c("2", "3")]
```

With the four lags together the associations sit on the day of exposure and
the day after. For days with both exposures the odds ratio is
`r pick("e11", "0")` at lag 0 and `r pick("e11", "1")` at lag 1; at lags 2
and 3 the odds ratios of the three categories lie between
`r fmt(min(later$or), 3)` and `r fmt(max(later$or), 3)`. With these definitions,
the associations that the single-lag models show at lags 2 and 3 are the
exposure of the days before, carried by its persistence. Over the four days
the cumulative odds
ratio is `r pick("e11", "cumulative")` for days with both exposures,
`r pick("e10", "cumulative")` for heatwave only and
`r pick("e01", "cumulative")` for high ozone only. A cumulative odds ratio
compares four consecutive days in the category with four consecutive days
with neither exposure.

### Interaction over the window

```{r}
#| label: tbl-compound-interaction
#| tbl-cap: "Additive and multiplicative interaction computed from the cumulative odds ratios (lags 0 to 3 together). REOI and AP have null value 0; S and the multiplicative ratio have null value 1."
t2 <- copy(lag_int)
# The causes are the columns: a factor fixes their order, and the header is
# taken from the reshaped table itself
t2[, `:=`(cause = factor(cause_labels[outcome], levels = cause_labels[unique(outcome)]),
          measure = factor(measure, levels = unique(measure)),
          value = ifelse(measure == "S" & (is.na(low) | high / low > 1e3),
                         paste(fmt(estimate, 3), "(interval not informative)"),
                         ci(estimate, low, high)))]
wide <- dcast(t2, measure ~ cause, value.var = "value")
kable(wide, col.names = c("Measure", names(wide)[-1]))
```

```{r}
#| label: interaction-text
reoi <- lag_int[measure == "REOI"]
```

The cumulative REOI is `r reoi[outcome == "non_accidental", ci(estimate, low, high)]`
for non-accidental mortality and
`r reoi[outcome == "cardiopulmonary", ci(estimate, low, high)]` for
cardiopulmonary mortality. Both intervals include zero: with the working
definitions there is no additive interaction at any lag or over the window.

### Across the definitions

The same model for the 15 heatwave definitions and the three cut-offs of the
delivered ozone series, fitted twice: as above, and with the temperature of
every lag in the model (the spline of the next section), to see whether an
interaction between the two indicators is temperature that the heatwave
threshold leaves out. The REOI of each lag comes from the three coefficients
of that lag; the cumulative REOI from the cumulative odds ratios.

```{r}
#| label: fig-grid
#| fig-cap: "REOI for non-accidental mortality from the model with all the lags, by lag and cumulative, across heatwave definitions (rows) and ozone cut-offs (columns), without and with temperature in the model. A dot marks the cells whose 95% interval excludes zero. Colour scale limited to plus or minus 0.15."
#| fig-height: 12.5
#| fig-width: 9.5
adjustment_labels <- c(none = "All lags in one model", temperature = "All lags and temperature")
g <- lag_grid[outcome == "non_accidental" & estimable == TRUE]
g[, `:=`(cutoff = paste0("> P", sub(".*_gt_p", "", ozone)),
         definition = factor(heatwave_label(heatwave),
                             levels = rev(heatwave_label(unique(lag_grid$heatwave)))),
         panel = factor(lag, levels = lag_levels, labels = c(paste("Lag", lags), "Cumulative")),
         fitted = factor(adjustment_labels[adjustment], levels = adjustment_labels),
         excludes_zero = low_reoi > 0 | high_reoi < 0)]
limit <- 0.15
ggplot(g, aes(cutoff, definition, fill = estimate_reoi)) +
  geom_tile(colour = ink$surface, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = g[excludes_zero == TRUE], size = 1.2, colour = ink$primary) +
  facet_grid(fitted ~ panel) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = diverging[["low"]], mid = diverging[["mid"]], high = diverging[["high"]],
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-limit, limit), oob = scales::squish, name = "REOI") +
  labs(x = "Ozone cut-off (municipality percentile)", y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), legend.position = "right",
        legend.justification = "center")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-grid
#| tbl-cap: "Cells of the grid (45 per cause) by the sign of the REOI and by whether its 95% interval lies above or below zero."
model_levels <- c("One lag per model", adjustment_labels)
count_cells <- function(dt, label) {
  dt[estimable == TRUE, .(model = label, positive = sum(estimate_reoi > 0), above = sum(low_reoi > 0),
                          below = sum(high_reoi < 0), median_reoi = median(estimate_reoi)),
     by = .(outcome, lag)]
}
one_lag <- single_grid[grepl(paste0("^", ozone_series, "_gt_p"), ozone) &
                         outcome %in% unique(lag_grid$outcome)]
one_lag[, lag := as.character(lag)]
cells <- rbind(count_cells(one_lag, "One lag per model"),
               count_cells(lag_grid[adjustment == "none"], adjustment_labels[["none"]]),
               count_cells(lag_grid[adjustment == "temperature"], adjustment_labels[["temperature"]]))
cells[, `:=`(cause = factor(cause_labels[outcome], levels = cause_labels[unique(outcome)]),
             lag = lag_factor(lag), model = factor(model, levels = model_levels))]
setorder(cells, cause, lag, model)
kable(cells[, .(cause, lag, model, positive, above, below, median_reoi)],
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 3),
      col.names = c("Cause", "Lag", "Model", "REOI above 0", "Interval above 0",
                    "Interval below 0", "Median REOI"))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-example
#| tbl-cap: "Odds ratios by lag in the cell with the clearest positive cumulative REOI, non-accidental mortality, all the lags in one model."
unadjusted <- lag_grid[outcome == "non_accidental" & estimable == TRUE & adjustment == "none"]
example <- unadjusted[lag == "cumulative"][which.max(low_reoi)]
example_rows <- unadjusted[heatwave == example$heatwave & ozone == example$ozone]
example_rows[, lag := lag_factor(lag)]
setorder(example_rows, lag)
kable(example_rows[, .(lag, ci(or_e01, or_low_e01, or_high_e01), ci(or_e10, or_low_e10, or_high_e10),
                       ci(or_e11, or_low_e11, or_high_e11), ci(estimate_reoi, low_reoi, high_reoi))],
      col.names = c("Lag", category_labels[["e01"]], category_labels[["e10"]],
                    category_labels[["e11"]], "REOI"))
```

```{r}
#| label: grid-text
n_cells <- function(model_value, lag_value, column) {
  cells[outcome == "non_accidental" & model == model_value & lag == lag_factor(lag_value)][[column]]
}
all_lags <- adjustment_labels[["none"]]
with_temperature <- adjustment_labels[["temperature"]]
cumulative_cells <- unadjusted[lag == "cumulative" & low_reoi > 0]
cumulative_cells[, threshold := sub("^hw_(.*)_[0-9]d$", "\\1", heatwave)]
working <- function(adjustment_value) {
  lag_grid[outcome == "non_accidental" & heatwave == heatwave_main & ozone == ozone_flag_main &
             lag == "cumulative" & adjustment == adjustment_value, ci(estimate_reoi, low_reoi, high_reoi)]
}
```

Fitting the lags together removes about half of the cells with a positive
interval at lags 2 and 3. For non-accidental mortality the single-lag models
give `r n_cells("One lag per model", "2", "above")` and
`r n_cells("One lag per model", "3", "above")` of 45 cells above zero at
lags 2 and 3; the model with all the lags gives
`r n_cells(all_lags, "2", "above")` and `r n_cells(all_lags, "3", "above")`,
and with temperature in the model `r n_cells(with_temperature, "2", "above")`
and `r n_cells(with_temperature, "3", "above")`.

Over the window the interaction does not disappear. The cumulative REOI is
positive in `r n_cells(all_lags, "cumulative", "positive")` of the 45 cells
(`r n_cells(with_temperature, "cumulative", "positive")` with temperature in
the model) and its interval lies above zero in
`r n_cells(all_lags, "cumulative", "above")`
(`r n_cells(with_temperature, "cumulative", "above")`). Of the
`r nrow(cumulative_cells)` cells above zero without temperature,
`r cumulative_cells[threshold %in% c("30c", "ehf"), .N]` use the 30 °C or the
EHF definitions, which have the most heatwave days. With the working
definition the cumulative REOI is `r working("none")`, and
`r working("temperature")` with temperature in the model: the same sign, with
an interval that includes zero.

The table shows the pattern in the cell
`r heatwave_label(example$heatwave)` with ozone above the
`r sub(".*_gt_p", "", example$ozone)`th percentile. On the day of exposure
the three categories have similar odds ratios and the REOI is close to zero.
Two and three days later the odds ratios of the days with one exposure are
below 1, most clearly for high ozone only, as if part of those deaths had been
brought forward by a few days, and those of the days with both are not. Over
the window the days with both exposures keep an excess that the days with one
exposure do not.

This is an exploratory result. It comes from
`r nrow(lag_grid[estimable == TRUE])` intervals without correction for
multiple comparisons, on definitions that share most of their days, so the
cells are not independent pieces of evidence, and it was not a hypothesis set
before looking at the data. On the day of exposure, where the associations
are strongest, there is no interaction; the positive values come from lags at
which the odds ratios are close to 1. It does not go away with temperature in
the model. Whether it can be reported as a finding depends on a primary
heatwave definition and lag window fixed in advance.

## Temperature

A distributed lag non-linear model (package `dlnm`) of the daily maximum
temperature, to see the association along the whole temperature scale instead
of at one threshold.

```{r}
#| label: thresholds
p95 <- thresholds[season_rule == get_param("temperature", "percentile_season")]
```

- **Scale.** The municipal series are area means: the 95th percentile of the
  daily maximum ranges from `r fmt(min(p95$p95), 1)` °C
  (`r p95[which.min(p95), municipality]`, which reaches into the Andes) to
  `r fmt(max(p95$p95), 1)` °C (`r p95[which.max(p95), municipality]`). A common
  curve in °C would compare places, not days. Temperature enters as the
  percentile of the day among the warm-season days of its municipality in
  the study years.
- **Shape.** Natural cubic spline with internal knots at the
  `r paste0(temperature$spline_knots, "th", collapse = " and ")` percentiles.
- **Lags.** `r min(lags)` to `r max(lags)`, one coefficient per lag for each
  spline term.
- **Odds ratios** are relative to the `r temperature$reference`th percentile.

```{r}
#| label: fig-curve
#| fig-cap: !expr 'sprintf("Cumulative odds ratio of death over lags %d to %d along the temperature scale, relative to the %dth percentile. Bands are 95%% confidence intervals.", min(lags), max(lags), temperature$reference)'
#| fig-height: 3.8
c1 <- curve[model == "temperature"]
c1[, cause := factor(cause_labels[outcome], levels = cause_labels[unique(outcome)])]
ggplot(c1, aes(percentile, or)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = ink$axis) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = or_low, ymax = or_high), fill = ramp_blue[2], alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(colour = ramp_blue[6], linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~cause) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 25, 50, 75, 90, 99)) +
  labs(x = "Daily maximum temperature (percentile of the municipality, warm season)",
       y = "Cumulative odds ratio")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-temperature-lags
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'sprintf("Odds ratios (95%% confidence interval) of temperature percentiles against the %dth percentile, by lag and cumulative.", temperature$reference)'
t3 <- temperature_or[model == "temperature"]
t3[, `:=`(cause = cause_labels[outcome], lag = lag_factor(lag), value = ci(or, or_low, or_high))]
kable(dcast(t3, cause + lag ~ paste0("P", percentile), value.var = "value"),
      col.names = c("Cause", "Lag", paste0("P", sort(unique(t3$percentile)))))
```

```{r}
#| label: temperature-text
cumulative <- temperature_or[model == "temperature" & lag == "cumulative" & outcome == "non_accidental"]
cum <- function(p) cumulative[percentile == p, ci(or, or_low, or_high)]
low_side <- curve[model == "temperature" & outcome == "non_accidental" & percentile < temperature$reference]
```

Below the median the curve is flat: the cumulative odds ratio stays between
`r fmt(min(low_side$or), 3)` and `r fmt(max(low_side$or), 3)`. Above it the
odds of death rise with temperature, to `r cum(90)` at the 90th percentile,
`r cum(95)` at the 95th and `r cum(99)` at the 99th for non-accidental
mortality. As with the categories, the association is in lags 0 and 1.

## Ozone as a continuous exposure

Ozone per `r ozone_increment` ppb of the delivered 24-hour mean, with one
coefficient per lag, alone and in the same model as the temperature
cross-basis.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ozone
#| fig-cap: !expr 'sprintf("Odds ratio of death per %d ppb of ozone by lag and cumulative, without and with temperature in the model. Bars are 95%% confidence intervals.", ozone_increment)'
#| fig-height: 3.8
o1 <- copy(ozone_or)
colour_adjust <- c("Ozone alone" = "#2a78d6", "Ozone and temperature" = "#eb6834")
o1[, `:=`(cause = factor(cause_labels[outcome], levels = cause_labels[unique(outcome)]),
          lag = lag_factor(lag),
          model = factor(fifelse(model == "ozone", "Ozone alone", "Ozone and temperature"),
                         levels = names(colour_adjust)))]
ggplot(o1, aes(lag, or, colour = model)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = ink$axis) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = or_low, ymax = or_high), position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
                  linewidth = 0.6, size = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~cause) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colour_adjust) +
  labs(x = "Lag (days)", y = sprintf("Odds ratio per %d ppb", ozone_increment), colour = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ozone
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'sprintf("Odds ratio per %d ppb of ozone (95%% confidence interval).", ozone_increment)'
o1[, value := ci(or, or_low, or_high)]
kable(dcast(o1, cause + lag ~ model, value.var = "value"),
      col.names = c("Cause", "Lag", levels(o1$model)))
```

```{r}
#| label: ozone-text
oz_cum <- function(outcome_value, model_value) {
  ozone_or[outcome == outcome_value & model == model_value & lag == "cumulative",
           ci(or, or_low, or_high)]
}
temp_with_ozone <- temperature_or[model == "temperature + ozone" & lag == "cumulative" &
                                    outcome == "non_accidental" & percentile == 95,
                                  ci(or, or_low, or_high)]
```

The cumulative odds ratio per `r ozone_increment` ppb for non-accidental
mortality goes from `r oz_cum("non_accidental", "ozone")` to
`r oz_cum("non_accidental", "temperature + ozone")` when temperature is in the
model, and for cardiopulmonary mortality from
`r oz_cum("cardiopulmonary", "ozone")` to
`r oz_cum("cardiopulmonary", "temperature + ozone")`. Most of the association
of the 24-hour ozone mean with mortality is shared with temperature. The
reverse does not happen: with ozone in the model the cumulative odds ratio of
the 95th temperature percentile is `r temp_with_ozone`, against `r cum(95)`
without it.

## What this adds

1. The associations with heatwaves and high ozone are on the day of exposure
   and the day after. Lags 2 and 3 taken alone mix them with the exposure of
   the days before.
2. With the working definitions the additive interaction is null at every
   lag, and over the window its interval includes zero.
3. Over the four-day window the REOI is positive in most combinations of
   definitions, and its interval excludes zero for those with the most
   heatwave days, with or without temperature in the model. It is exploratory
   and needs a primary definition and lag window fixed in advance.
4. Temperature has a clear association with mortality above the median of the
   warm season, rising up to the hottest days.
5. The association of the 24-hour ozone mean is largely shared with
   temperature. This bears on the secondary aim of the plan, the mediation of
   the heat effect by ozone, which has not been analysed here: an ozone
   association this small once temperature is accounted for leaves little
   room for a large mediated share.

These readings rest on the delivered 24-hour ozone series. The
[validation of the ozone exposure](deliverable_1_exposure.html#sec-ozone-validation)
shows that it follows the hourly records less well on the days with most
ozone; the same models can be run on the rebuilt series by changing
`ozone_series_main` in the configuration.

## Method checks

*Script: `tests/test_methods.R`, run here and at the start of every run of
`Code/run_all.R`.*

```{r}
#| label: method-checks
#| code-summary: "Run tests/test_methods.R"
checks <- system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"),
                  shQuote(here::here("tests", "test_methods.R")), stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE)
if (!is.null(attr(checks, "status"))) stop(paste(checks, collapse = "\n"))
cat(grep("distributed lags|dlnm|cumulative|all lags|combine_coefficients|local_percentile|^All",
         checks, value = TRUE), sep = "\n")
```

The checks simulate deaths with an effect at lags 0 and 1 only: the model with
all the lags recovers it, and the single-lag model at lag 2 reports an
association that is not there. They also confirm that the cross-basis of
`dlnm` and a spline built by hand for each lag give the same cumulative odds
ratios.

# Publication figures {#sec-publication-figures}

*Script: `Code/50_figures_publication.R`. Figures: the files `figure_*` of
`Output/Figures`, each as PDF and as PNG.*

`Code/50_figures_publication.R` draws the figures from the saved tables, as
PDF and as PNG at `r get_param("figures", "png_dpi")` dpi, in `Output/Figures`. The
button under each figure saves the PNG file; the PDF files are in
[`Output/Figures`](https://github.com/AmaruSimonAgueroJimenez/Heatwave-ozone-mortality-Chile/tree/main/Output/Figures) of the repository.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-figures
#| tbl-cap: "Files written by the figures script."
figure_content <- c(
  figure_1_odds_ratios_by_lag = "Odds ratios of the exposure categories by lag",
  figure_2_reoi_by_cause = "Forest plot of the REOI by cause of death",
  figure_3_interaction_matrix = "REOI across heatwave definitions and ozone cut-offs, non-accidental",
  figure_4_subgroups = "Age groups and sex",
  figure_5_attributable_deaths = "Excess deaths by year and by municipality",
  figure_6_lag_structure = "Single-lag and distributed-lag estimates",
  figure_7_adjustment = "Multi-pollutant adjustment",
  figure_s1_interaction_matrix_cardiopulmonary = "REOI across definitions, cardiopulmonary",
  figure_s2_interaction_matrix_all_lags = "REOI across definitions, all the lags in one model",
  figure_s3_interaction_matrix_all_lags_temperature = "The same, with temperature in the model"
)
# Every figure the script wrote is in the list, and every figure of the list was written
written <- sub("\\.pdf$", "", sort(list.files(dir_figures, pattern = "^figure_.*\\.pdf$")))
stopifnot(setequal(written, names(figure_content)),
          file.exists(file.path(dir_figures, paste0(names(figure_content), ".png"))))
kable(data.table(file = sprintf("`%s.pdf` and `.png`", names(figure_content)), content = unname(figure_content)),
      col.names = c("File", "Content"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-publication
#| fig-cap: !expr 'sprintf("%s. File `%s.png`.", figure_content, names(figure_content))'
#| out-width: "100%"
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(dir_figures, paste0(names(figure_content), ".png")))
```
